side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 Owners active within the window, after the ratchet; every member recomputes it, else census_expected_active_mismatch.
side_b: CC 3.1.3 `active_count` (owners active in at least one of the last four periods)
note: Is active_count the raw count of owners whose recent bit is set, or the ratcheted base? CC 6.1.9 and CC 3.1.3 make it the raw count ("that count under a ratchet" is the base, computed after); CC 2.6.1.7 and its floor_applied row make it the value after the ratchet. A member recomputing one refuses the other as census_expected_active_mismatch. C156 names this as its part b; the wording of CC 2.6.1.7 is still there.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 The bit is set when the owner was active in this period or any of the previous three. It is not something recoverable from a sum.
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json reads=census:member:partial&last(4); over=active/owner; combine=count(owner)
note: The text has the owner compute its own four-period bit and every member recompute the count "from the two partials" of the period. The fold cell (and the CC 8.10 card) reads the last four periods of partials and counts owners, which a sum cannot give and which counts an owner once per period it reported. The window is in the bit, not in the fold. The census model README says the same as the text.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 It is released by the first period whose count is at least two thirds of the count before the fall
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json test=count*3>=prev*2 ?open:frozen
note: The text freezes on a fall against the count before it (prev) and releases against the count before the fall (ref), a fixed reference. The fold cell has one test against prev. Read period by period, a base frozen by a fall from 30 to 10 is released the next period at 10 (10*3 >= 10*2), where the text holds it until a period returns 20. The same cell list also uses prev for the previous base in the ratchet term.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 `max_source_multiplicity` is `1` on every census composite by construction
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 The largest multiplicity cluster; aggregation_meta_multiplicity above the floor.
note: CC 6.1.9 goes on: "the census door refuses any other value". CC 2.6.1.7 and the refusal list of CC 3.1.3 apply only the R9 gate (multiplicity times n_min at most source_count), so a composite carrying 2 over a large source_count is admitted under one reading and refused under the other. No refusal token is named for the CC 6.1.9 rule.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 Distinct owners behind the composite; below 10 the cell is refused census_composite_below_k.
side_b: CC 3.1.3 refusals `ballot_tally_partials_mismatch`, `ballot_tally_mass_total_mismatch`, `ballot_tally_duplicate_period`, `aggregation_meta_dominated`
note: Does the floor of ten apply to a community's secret poll? The source_count row of CC 2.6.1.7 is REQUIRED on census:composite and ballot:tally and states the refusal for both. The ballot:tally row of CC 3.1.3 lists no below-k refusal and CC 6.1.9 gives a tally only the dominance gate. A room of six that holds a poll gets a result under one reading and a refused tally under the other. The census model closes its tally instances at K = 2.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 A silent member is not in the denominator. The tally is taken over **who shows up**
side_b: CC 4.5.13 The base is the standing roster at or below the count minimum the governance policy table pins and, above it, the expected-active count
note: The fallback vote on a moderation action is counted over the members who voted on that proposal in one paragraph, and over the census base in another. The policy row moderation_action has base active and floor 1/2, and CC 6.1 calls the base "a denominator a community's rules read". With 3 of 40 expected-active members voting, 2 keep-votes carry under the first and fail under the second. The census model names the first reading (ThresholdBase = responders) as the one its invariant refuses.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 The expected-active count is the community's own member-only census composite
side_b: data manifests/governance_policy.json base(N) = N if N <= k else max(min, k + (N - k) // tail); rows with base=standing use N
note: The data's base law computes the base from the roster size alone (k 12, tail 30, min 3: a roster of 100 gives 14) and its decider reads that. The text takes the base above the count minimum from the census, under the ratchet of CC 6.1.9. The data marks its law provisional and the text says "the law's constants are provisional until measured", but the two are different functions, and an implementation that replays the decider as CC 4.5.13 tells it to never reads census:expected_active.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 The floor is the standing roster at or below the count minimum of the
side_b: data manifests/governance_policy.json "min_count": {
note: The count minimum the governance policy table pins has two candidates in the data: min_count (community 2, self 1), which the decider uses as the fewest voices, and base_law.k (12), the roster size up to which the base is the roster. A reader who takes the named one gives rooms of 3 to 12 the census base; the base law gives them the roster. The census model README calls it "the small-community size".

side_a: CC 6.1.9 Counts of the mesh — nodes, links, rows held — count nodes, at most eight per owner.
side_b: CC 6.1.9 one return per owner is one source
note: C154 was read as no conflict on the ground that the return token is one per owner per period. CC 2.6.1.7 derives it from the node: "H(node_secret ‖ period)". With per-node tokens the duplicate-token refusal admits up to eight returns per owner, mass_total is then the number of returns, and the checks "mass_total = source_count" and source_count as "Distinct owners behind the composite" cannot both hold. Whether a second node of one owner is counted or dropped is not decided by the text.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.3 per-node composites publish the median bucket, which moves at most one bucket below a fifth of returns forged
side_b: CC 6.1.9 A composite is a histogram per field per cell. A reader computes the median bucket and the trimmed statistics from it
note: Part 1 has the composite publish a median; CC 6.1.9 has it publish the whole histogram with exact field sums and leaves the median to the reader (the family fold says by=reader). CC 6.1.9 governs.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 Merkle root over the accepted tokens; a contributor checks its token's path against it
side_b: CC 6.1.9 A contributor recomputes `member_commitment` over the published member list and compares.
note: One check needs an inclusion path served to the contributor, the other a published list of every accepted token. CC 1.13.3.3 follows CC 6.1.9 ("over the published list"). No row is named that carries the list.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.8 a statement whose content is low-entropy, a ballot or a census cell, carries a random salt as a payload member
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json "member": "salt", "type": "bstr .size 16", "presence": "required", "in_cddl": true, "cc_ref": "CC 2.6.1.8"
note: The family model requires salt today on census:share, census:member:share and ballot:tally, and not on census:composite, the partials or census:expected_active. The text states the salt only for the planned form of CC 2.6.1.8, and the signed-object table of CC 2.6.1.7 has no salt row. A share is uniformly random already; the low-entropy rows are the composite, the tally and the expected-active count.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 `census_composite_duplicate_period` (a second composite for the class and period, from any seat)
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json "verbs": {"value": ["attest", "replace", "withdraw"], "source": "cc-table"
note: The family row and its CC 8.10 card give a composite (and a partial, and census:expected_active) a supersede by its author. The text refuses any second composite for a class and period, and the fold of the same family says pick=once. A reader of the text resolves it for the refusal.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 the floor is the larger of the roster's rooted-active members and half of the last stable count
side_b: data formal/census_ballot/README.md `max(owners active this period, ⌈½ · last stable composite⌉)`
note: Rooted-active members is used once and not defined. The model reads it as owners active in this period; it could be read as the expected-active (four-period) members who chain to a root. The model notes the first arm is subsumed by base >= count either way, so the outcome is the same.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 an **addressed** row whose signed `for_key_id` is one of the period's two serve seats
side_b: CC 6.1.9 The door checks only that `for_key_id` names a serve seat, refusing otherwise (`census_return_recipient_not_seat`), never membership in the drawn pair.
note: Read as no conflict in the table. The registry row still describes the recipient as one of the drawn pair, while its own refusal list has only the not-a-seat refusal. CC 6.1.9 governs.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 0 or 1: which of the two additive shares, and which aggregator's partial. Any other value is census_share_index_invalid.
side_b: CC 3.1.3 `ballot_share_duplicate_token` and `ballot_share_pair_incomplete` as for the census share.
note: The member-share rows take ballot_* names for two refusals in CC 3.1.3 and census_* names for the index and the expiry (census_return_expired) in CC 2.6.1.7. Which token a member share with index 2, or one offered late, is refused by is not stated for the family.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 a cell with fewer than **k = 10** owners is merged upward and then withheld as *below the floor* (`census_composite_below_k`)
side_b: CC 6.1.9 The door refuses a composite with fewer than **k = 10** sources (`census_composite_below_k`).
note: One token names a door refusal of a whole row (CC 3.1.3: source_count < 10) and a cell withheld inside a published row. CC 2.6.1.7 says "the cell is refused". A reader resolves it as: aggregators merge small cells before publishing, the door refuses a row whose source_count is under ten.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 a first-run or consent item runs the self row, one voice of one, no window
side_b: data manifests/choice_item.cddl (self_choice for a first-run or consent item)
note: The text says the item's policy is "a row of the governance policy table above". The table has no self row with no window: its two self rows are the self-roster add and evict, 86 400 s, one voice a key. The CDDL names the policy self_choice and manifests/transitions.json names it selfAct; neither is a row of constitution/governance_policy.tsv. A validator that requires a table row refuses every first-run item.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 **Announcing starts on,** its cost on screen.
side_b: CC 5.4.6 So a node whose owner resolves to the `minor` band MUST NOT carry a federation-scope owner-binding
note: To fix from the text, and not yet fixed: the default-on sentence of CC 4.5.13 still carries no exception for an owner with no age assurance on record, who reads as under 13. The same paragraph's rule "A default is otherwise admissible only for a choice that narrows or keeps things as they are" stands beside it.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 REQUIRED on consent:state:granted and on delegates_to
side_b: CC 3.3.1 A `granted` naming no scope matches nothing, by design.
note: Is a grant with no scope refused at the door or admitted as a grant of nothing? CC 2.1 says both in one row. CC 2.6.1.2 lists scope with the optional members ("absent", "member absent"), unlike its rows for required members, which read "on one, admission refuses". CC 3.3.5 admits a consent_record with stance granted on three required fields, scope not among them. The family model's body for consent:state has no required scope. The text leans to admitted and matching nothing; the signed-object table says required.

side_a: CC 3.3.1 Closed-set stance values; `revoked` overrides prior `granted`.
side_b: CC 3.1.5 `{stance}` ∈ `granted` \| `revoked` \| `expired` — closed; `expired` is the one substrate-emitted value.
note: The CC 3.3.1 row is headed `consent:state:{granted\|revoked}` and calls that set closed; CC 3.1.5, CC 3.3.5 and the registry (three values, open false) add expired, emitted by the substrate when valid_until passes. A door built from CC 3.3.1 refuses a peer substrate's consent:state:expired row as outside a closed vocabulary. The registry supports three.

side_a: CC 2.1 | `expires_at` | `membership:proposal`, REQUIRED |
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 REQUIRED on census:share:{class}:v1 and census:member:share:v1, where it is the period's end
note: The signed-object table gives expires_at as OPTIONAL and names the families where it is required: the two census shares only. CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.2 require it on a membership proposal ("on one, admission refuses") and CC 3.1.3 on a lineage_witness proposal ("with a required `expires_at`"). The family model carries the membership requirement with presence "unstated". A door driven by the table admits an invitation that never expires.

side_a: CC 2.1 | `role` | `membership:proposal`, nullable; restated on `membership:acceptance` |
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 an explicit JSON null on any optional member is refused federation_malformed_row / envelope_member_null
note: Nullable in CC 2.1, "`null` (no role offered)" in CC 2.6.1.2 and "key_id | null", "null = indefinite" in the consent_record block of CC 3.3.5 read as a member written with JSON null. CC 2.6.1.7 says for oversight_mode that null means absent and that a written null is refused; it does not say so for role. A producer that writes "role": null has its proposal refused.

Registered families use references_attestation_id on scores rows (membership and lineage-witness answers, deferral responses, the build attestation), which CC 3.1.2.1 allows; CC 2.6.1.7 reads the member only by row type on the three composers, and CC 3.5 defines a standalone attestation as one with no `references_attestation_id`. note: The conformance class has a producer declare both members; CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.7 make both optional, absent reading as external and as the per-cell default. A producer that omits them is conformant under the tables and not under the class sentence read strictly. The tables govern admission.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7 The `{scale}` vocabulary above has seven tokens.
side_b: data manifests/namespace_registry.json "open": true, "segment": "{scale}", "values": ["self"]
note: The registry, generated from the Part 3 table, holds one of the seven scale tokens (the row separates them with commas where other rows use bars) and marks the vocabulary open. The text lists seven and forbids adding federation; it does not call the set closed, so by CC 3.1.7 it is open, and the forbidden token is admitted by the registry.

note: The section says the key-suffixed spelling is for readability and is never emitted, then says the substrate emits it. The first sentence and CC 3.1.9.4 govern: the dimension is hard_case:family_membership_change and the key is in the payload.
